subject: Multi-cloud offer planning: SKU compression, regional gating & co-sell readiness
messages:
From: Amit Patel <amit.p@cloudworks.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.s@aws-partner.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace packaging question: single vs multiple SKUs per cloud

Grace — thanks for the walkthrough last week. We need to lock the final SKU/region plan for the three cloud marketplaces so our legal/compliance and marketplace ops teams can start the listing workflows. High level asks from our side:

- One-page SKU matrix that shows plan names, meter type (hourly/consumption), and which regions each plan will be published in per cloud.
- Any cloud-specific constraints (image vs. SaaS listing, billing model differences) called out.
- Which SKUs we should gate initially vs. broad launch.

Can you or your team share a recommended split? We have a tight timeline — marketplace onboarding needs to start by 22 Feb to hit co-sell enablement windows in March.

I attached a short doc with our internal requirements (CW_Marketplace_requirements.docx). Happy to jump on a short sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Amit

CloudWorks Inc.

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit.p@cloudworks.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Maya Singh <maya.s@aws-partner.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging question: single vs multiple SKUs per cloud

Amit — thanks, got the doc. I pushed an initial SKU matrix and notes to the Drive and attached a working copy (SKU_pack_matrix_v3.xlsx) for your review. High-level recommendation from the product + GTM side: compress offers into three canonical tiers and then apply cloud-specific region gating and plan flavors. Rationale: minimizes bookkeeping for partner co-sell, reduces listing churn, and keeps pricing/packaging consistent for customers moving between clouds.

Recommended approach (short):
- Offer tiers: Core (small), Scale (medium), Enterprise (large). Each tier represents a bundle of throughput and token quotas rather than instance sizes.
- AWS: launch Core+Scale in all commercial regions; Enterprise in top 5 regions (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1) to keep latency/SLA guarantees and co-sell eligibility. Metering: hourly + token-based metered add-ons for high-throughput.
- Azure: start with US & EU regions (eastus, westeurope) for initial listing. Azure requires distinct plan IDs per SKU so we'll publish the same three tiers as separate plans under one offer. Metering: plan-level metering (managed by marketplace) — recommend keeping fewer plans to reduce plan-level billing mapping.
- GCP: curated regions only (us-central1, europe-west1) for initial phase due to quota & marketplace agent constraints. Consider a single image with billing mapping in Offer/Plan metadata to avoid multiple images.

Cloud-specific considerations to call out:
- Azure requires separate plan IDs and has stricter publisher verification for enterprise plans.
- AWS co-sell requires meeting minimum usage and listing metadata for partner managers; tagging + per-customer onboarding flow needs to be encoded.
- GCP marketplace often needs a tighter packaging approach (managed SaaS vs bring-your-own-image tradeoffs).

Attachments & artifacts: SKU_pack_matrix_v3.xlsx, co-sell_playbook_notes.pdf (draft).

Open questions / asks for CloudWorks:
1) Confirm whether CloudWorks needs metered tokens exposed as a line-item vs packaged in a single monthly meter.
2) Any geo-restrictions for data residency that would force region exclusions?
3) Do you want us to start the AWS co-sell packet now (we can submit the offer draft to your partner manager) or wait until Azure is ready too?

Proposed next steps: internal sign-off by Redwood (Ben + Karthik) by EOD Tue 16 Feb, then a quick 30-min sync with your ops on Wed 17 Feb to walk the matrix and finalize the first submission. If that works I’ll schedule.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

On Sun, Feb 14, 2027 at 11:03 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Amit — thanks, got the doc. I pushed an initial SKU matrix and notes to the Drive and attached a working copy (SKU_pack_matrix_v3.xlsx) for your review.

Quick technical/cost constraints from infra/model-serving side (call these must-haves we need to encode in the SKU matrix):

- Single image, multiple plans: easiest for ops if we ship one container image and control SKU via plan metadata and config flags. Azure forces separate plan IDs (fine) but avoid publishing separate VM images per plan.
- Metering granularity: AWS supports hourly + custom metering APIs for token usage; GCP uses a different billing path that can be slower to reconcile. Recommend: package a monthly committed unit (e.g., tokens/month) for Core/Scale/Enterprise and expose optional metered add-ons only for Enterprise customers to limit reconciliation complexity.
- Latency SLAs: Enterprise SKUs must be pinned to dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) in the listing copy. That affects pricing and regions (we can only promise pinned capacity in select regions).
- Quantization/CPU tradeoffs: for Scale tier we should default to 8-bit quant models to balance cost for customers; list quantization profile in plan metadata so partner ops knows expected perf.
- Integration hooks: include a small webhook URL in the offer metadata so we can validate provisioning requests and map marketplace customer IDs to our internal account IDs.

I’ll update the SKU_pack_matrix_v3 with the above and mark the rows that require dedicated capacity and which can live on hosted API.

Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging question: single vs multiple SKUs per cloud

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful. A few quick confirmations from CloudWorks side:

- We prefer the compressed three-tier model (Core/Scale/Enterprise). It simplifies procurement and co-sell collateral.
- For metering, we want token usage visible as an add-on line-item for customers, but for the initial marketplace submission we can bundle tokens into the monthly unit to accelerate approval.
- Data residency: CloudWorks needs EU data residency for enterprise customers — so please mark EU regions as Enterprise-eligible only unless otherwise agreed.

Next steps: Please send the finalized matrix + a one-page summary for our legal/ops by EOD Wed 17 Feb. Also agree to a 30-min call Wed 17 Feb 10:00 PT to finalize the AWS packet — Maya, can you join briefly so we can confirm co-sell checklist items?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Amit
Director, Cloud Partnerships
CloudWorks Inc.
